problem: The five-whys Claude Code plugin (v0.1.0) is rated only 6/10 instead of 10/10. The plugin asks "why" five levels deep with five reasons per step (3,905 reasons), fanned out as one root sub-agent (levels 1-2) plus 25 parallel branch sub-agents (levels 3-5, 155 reasons each), with a Python script that shape-validates fragments and assembles one line-per-reason JSON file (~150k tokens) meant to be read into context whole; analysis is left to the user. The rating reflects: no full real run yet, shape-only validation with no content-quality or duplication checks, isolated branch agents that likely repeat causes, probable quality decay at depth 5, a heavy ~150k-token output, and default-model cost, a hard-coded 5x5 shape, and no tests or evals.
reading: Top-level whys answer 'Why does the problem occur?'. Each node's whys answer 'Why <that node's reason>?'. An id is the dotted path from the top, so 2.4.1 is the 1st reason for 2.4, which is the 4th reason for 2.
